name: General Work Visa

requirement_groups.name: Employer-sponsored, labour-market test, occupation not on Critical Skills List

requirements.blocker_text: Requires a job offer from a South African employer for a role not appearing on the Critical Skills List, together with a certificate from the Department of Employment and Labour confirming the employer could not find a suitably qualified South African citizen or permanent resident for the role after a diligent recruitment search.
requirements.fix_path: Secure a job offer from a South African employer willing to complete the Department of Employment and Labour certification process.

evidence_required.document: Department of Employment and Labour certificate confirming no suitable local candidate was found
Police clearance, medical and radiology reports

outcome.duration_length: up to 5 years, tied to the employment contract, renewable

sources.title: Employsome -- Work Permit South Africa 2026: 6 Visa Types & TES Fast-Track, describing the General Work Visa's Department of Employment and Labour certification requirement and the DHA backlog affecting processing times (6-12 months)

notes: STATUS: DRAFT. HONEST SOURCING GAP: no direct fetch of a dha.gov.za or Department of Employment and Labour page was achieved for this route in this research pass. STRUCTURAL CONTRAST worth stating plainly against za_critical_skills_visa: this is the genuine labour-market-tested counterpart to Critical Skills' no-job-offer-required, points-based structure -- the General Work Visa requires an actual job offer plus a formal Department of Employment and Labour certification that no local candidate could be found, a materially heavier and slower burden. Sources checked describe persistent Department of Home Affairs processing backlogs pushing standard General Work Visa timelines to 6-12 months as of 2026, a real operational reality distinct from the formal legal requirements documented here. pr_after_months (60) reflects the direct-residence Section 26(a) track requiring 5 years continuously on a qualifying work visa plus a permanent (open-ended, no fixed end date) employment offer -- a specific 'permanent means no contractual end date' distinction confirmed by a separate source consulted for za_permanent_residence, worth flagging since a fixed-term renewal contract, however long, does not satisfy this test.
